How many parameters in a 3×3 conv layer from 32 to 64 channels?
Why use CNNs instead of dense layers for images?
a: Local connectivity and weight sharing: each filter looks at a small patch and is reused at every position. That cuts parameters massively, uses the spatial structure of images, and detects a feature wherever it appears (translation equivariance).

q: Why stack two 3×3 convolutions instead of one 5×5?
a: Same 5×5 receptive field, fewer parameters (2 × 9C² = 18C² vs 25C²) and an extra non-linearity, so more expressive. Three 3×3 layers match a 7×7 (27C² vs 49C²).

Downsamples feature maps (e.g. 2×2 max pool halves height and width), reducing computation and adding some translation invariance. Global average pooling collapses each channel to one number before the classifier, replacing large dense layers.
It mixes information across channels at each pixel, acting like a dense layer per position. Used to reduce or expand channel counts cheaply (ResNet bottlenecks, Inception) and add non-linearity.

Convolutions are translation equivariant: shift the input, the feature map shifts. Pooling adds partial invariance. Full invariance isn't guaranteed (striding and boundaries break it), so shift/crop augmentation still helps.

q: How would you build an image classifier with only 2,000 labelled images?
a: Transfer learning: take a pretrained backbone (ResNet, EfficientNet, ViT), replace the head, freeze the backbone and train the head with strong augmentation; then unfreeze the top blocks with a small learning rate if validation improves. Use stratified validation and early stopping.
